name: Kingdom of Hejaz
summary: A kingdom in western Arabia created when Sharif Hussein of Mecca led the Arab Revolt against the Ottomans (1916); Ibn Saud conquered it in 1924–25.

knownFor.label: Arab Revolt
knownFor.note: Uprising against the Ottomans with British help.

knownFor.label: Hejaz Railway
knownFor.note: Raided by T. E. Lawrence and Arab fighters.

location.value: The Hejaz region, the western part of the Arabian Peninsula.

terrain.value: Coastal plain (Tihama) and the Hejaz mountains.

resources.value: Income from the Hajj pilgrimage; little farming.

population.value: Not stated for the kingdom. The infobox gives 10.5 million (2011) for the wider Hejaz region.

disease.value: Cholera and other epidemics spread among pilgrims.

migration.value: Tens of thousands of Hajj pilgrims every year.

tradeRoutes.value: Jeddah port and the Hejaz Railway (damaged in the war).

wealth.value: Poor; dependent on pilgrims and British money.

moneyAndTax.value: Pilgrim taxes and British gold sovereigns.

inequality.value: Sharifian elite and merchants above Bedouin tribes.

governmentType.value: An absolute monarchy under the Hashemite dynasty: Hussein bin Ali (1916–1924) and Ali bin Hussein (1924–1925). The page does not describe a formal guardianship of Mecca and Medina, and Medina stayed under Ottoman control.

keyRulers.value: Hussein bin Ali reigned from 10 June 1916 until he abdicated on 3 October 1924; Ali bin Hussein reigned until he was deposed on 19 December 1925. The infobox lists different rulers, so the page is inconsistent.

succession.value: Hussein abdicated in favour of Ali (1924).

institutions.value: Few modern institutions; a small cabinet.

armyAndTech.value: Tribal fighters with British arms and advisers.

majorWars.value: Hussein proclaimed the Great Arab Revolt against the Ottomans (Medina stayed Ottoman throughout; the page gives no end date); the British withdrew support in favour of Ibn Saud, the Nejd conquered the kingdom on 19 December 1925, and Abdulaziz was crowned King of Hejaz on 8 January 1926.

alliancesRivals.value: Allied with Britain; rival of Ibn Saud.

scienceEducation.value: Religious schools in Mecca and Medina.

openness.value: Open to pilgrims from around the world.

communicationTransport.value: Camels, ships and the damaged railway.

religion.value: Sunni Islam, with Arabic as the common language.

artsArchitecture.value: Hejazi coral-stone houses with wooden screens (rawasheen).

dailyLife.value: Town life organised around the pilgrimage.

ideasReligions.value: Pan-Arab hopes; Hussein claimed the caliphate (1924).

riseSignals.value: An independent State of Hejaz under Sharif Hussein bin Ali was proclaimed in 1916, after Ottoman control ended.

peakPeriod.value: The page gives no peak. It was self-proclaimed as a kingdom in June 1916 and recognised on 10 August 1920; Britain then backed Ibn Saud, and Hussein surrendered on 23 December 1925 (the infobox says 19 December).

declineSignals.value: Hussein claimed the caliphate (1924), angering many.

outcome.value: Hussein surrendered to the Saudis on 23 December 1925. The article gives 1925 for incorporation and 23 September 1932 for the renaming to Saudi Arabia.

overallCertainty.value: Main events are well documented; population figures are estimates.
